text:
Thirteen wins in 19 games and 27 points (a .710 points percentage) for Marco Sturm's Bruins, and our playoff race gives them an 81% chance to get in. The honest footnote: by chance quality they've been an even team. Their expected goals share is 50.6%, and they have about six more points than their chances earned.

The gap has a name. Michael DiPietro, whose development stalled for years in Vancouver, has stopped .930 over his last five starts (4-0-0), 5.5 goals better than expected. As a team Boston has allowed 13.8 fewer goals than the shots against predicted. Goalie heaters are the least reliable thing in hockey.

What is real is the top pair. Hampus Lindholm and Charlie McAvoy own 63% of the expected goals at 5-on-5 and have been on for 12 goals for, five against. David Pastrnak and Pavel Zacha keep producing beside JJ Peterka.

The worries are piling up. Rookie James Hagens went on injured reserve with a back injury after the Pittsburgh game and is expected to miss a few weeks and breaks up a line that had outscored opponents 8-3. Nikita Zadorov's opening-faceoff fight with Brady Tkachuk set the tone for a 4-1 win over Florida, but Thursday's 5-2 loss to Montreal in their first game back home was flat; Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub noted Cole Caufield has 12 goals in a 12-game stretch against Boston. Watch the save percentage: when it cools, we'll learn what this team is.
headline: Sturm's Bruins are winning faster than they're playing
